title: OpenAI Strict Functions and Structured Output
summary: Choose between Responses structured text and strict function calls, define constrained schemas, validate semantics, and keep execution under application control.
prerequisites: An OpenAI model that supports the selected feature
A JSON Schema for the intended data
Node.js 22 and PowerShell 7 for the offline lab

sections.title: Choose the correct control
paragraphs: Use a Responses text.format object with type json_schema when the model should produce a schema-constrained answer. Use a function tool when the model should request an application capability. Structured response controls answer shape. It does not execute a function, authorize a user, or establish that generated content is true. JSON-object mode is weaker because it guarantees JSON but not conformance to a supplied schema.

For tools, the application must allowlist the function name, parse and validate arguments, make a separate authorization decision from trusted context, and execute only after every check passes. This lesson uses a read-only synthetic stock fixture. It performs no market lookup, purchase, sale, or other external side effect.

sections.title: Define an explicit Responses contract
paragraphs: These are provider-shaped Responses request bodies. The structured answer places type, name, strict, and schema under text.format. The tool places type, name, description, strict, and parameters in tools. OpenAI supports a subset of JSON Schema, so confirm that a deployment supports every keyword used by its contract.

The tool schema describes ticker and quantity, but the application repeats the important checks locally. Provider schema matching is not authorization, tool allowlisting, semantic correctness, or execution permission. The model placeholder is deliberate because no current model name was established for this resource.

code.label: Provider-shaped request bodies

sections.title: Follow the provider call and result correlation
paragraphs: This filled exchange is a synthetic fixture shaped like a Responses function-call lifecycle. It is not a live OpenAI response, a market quote, or a receipt. The function-call output item has an item id, fc_item_fixture_001, and a distinct call_id, call_fixture_001. The application correlates its function_call_output with call_id, never with the item id.

The application accepts the call only after the response is complete, no provider error or refusal is present, the tool is allowlisted, the arguments parse, local shape and domain checks pass, trusted authorization permits the read, and call_id equals the separately trusted expected identifier. It then serializes the synthetic result into output.

code.label: Synthetic provider response and correlated application submission

sections.title: Separate six different controls
paragraphs: A structured response is an answer the provider was asked to shape with text.format. Schema validation checks JSON syntax, object shape, required fields, types, and prohibited keys. Semantic validation checks meaning, such as whether a ticker belongs to the synthetic domain and whether quantity is an integer from 1 through 100. Tool allowlisting limits dispatch to explicitly registered application functions.

Authorization asks whether the authenticated caller and trusted context may perform the operation. Execution is the actual application action after all preceding checks. These controls are not interchangeable. A schema-valid call can name an unregistered tool, violate a business rule, lack permission, or be unsafe to execute.

code.label: Trust boundary order
code.code:
provider completion, error, refusal
  -> obtain function_call and actual call_id
  -> compare with separately trusted expectedCallId
  -> allowlist tool name
  -> parse arguments
  -> schema and shape validation
  -> semantic validation
  -> authorization from trusted context
  -> bounded execution
  -> serialized function_call_output with the actual call_id

sections.title: Adapt an actual Responses lifecycle without inventing statuses
paragraphs: Raw Responses data should be adapted before the domain validator runs. The adapter below handles response.error, an incomplete response, refusal content, absence of a completed lifecycle, missing calls, and ambiguous multiple calls. It preserves the actual call_id but receives expectedCallId and authorization separately from trusted application state.

A refusal is represented as typed refusal content, not as an invented normal status named refused. The adapter does not parse arguments or execute the tool. buildFunctionOutput creates the provider-shaped result only after processEnvelope succeeds.

code.label: adapter.mjs

sections.title: Set up the complete offline Node.js 22 lab
paragraphs: Save this as setup.ps1 and run it with PowerShell 7 from a parent directory. It refuses an existing target directory. It creates a used stocks.json fixture, the adapter, a deliberately flawed learner implementation, an independent immutable test file, a repaired implementation, and a separate reference implementation. No package installation, network connection, cloud credential, or real side effect is required.

The normalized event passed to processEnvelope is an application boundary object produced after lifecycle inspection. expectedCallId and authorized belong to a separate context object and are never copied from the untrusted call. The tests freeze their case data, gather every result, use deep equality, and convert a crash into a failing CRASH result rather than accepting a thrown exception as a valid rejection.

code.label: setup.ps1

sections.title: Run the baseline and inspect the exact evidence
paragraphs: Run the baseline from the created directory. In the recorded Node.js 22 execution dated 2026-09-20, 9 of 12 cases passed and exactly three failed: unknownKey, arrayValue, and range. nullValue, wrongCorrelation, refusal, and incomplete passed. The command exited with code 1.

The test suite is evidence about this implementation, not an ultimate specification or proof of production safety. Its cases remain separate from student.mjs and should not be edited during the repair. A learner must also reason about lifecycle handling, authorization, missing call identifiers, and other boundaries represented in the implementation.

code.label: Baseline command and exact recorded output

sections.title: Make one coherent boundary repair
paragraphs: Repair student.mjs at the argument-validation boundary rather than copying the complete reference. First, change the object check to reject arrays explicitly. Second, reject every key except ticker and quantity. Third, require an integer quantity and enforce that ticker exists in the loaded fixture and quantity is from 1 through 100. These changes address the three observed failures as one lesson: provider promises do not replace local boundary validation.

repaired.mjs contains that completed repair while retaining the existing lifecycle, correlation, allowlist, authorization, and fixture execution path. reference.mjs is independently written and produces the same decisions. Both read stocks.json, so the declared fixture is the actual source of unit prices.

code.label: The focused replacement after JSON.parse

sections.title: Verify the repaired and reference results
paragraphs: Run both commands without changing tests.mjs. The repaired command has 12 passes, no failures, and exit code 0. The separate reference also has 12 passes, no failures, and exit code 0. The complete repaired output is shown below. The reference prints the same twelve lines and TOTAL line because its returned values are deeply equal.

Passing this suite establishes only the behavior of these offline cases. It does not establish a live provider response, current market value, complete security review, or authorization for a real deployment.

code.label: Exact repaired output and reference command result

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: valid accepts ACME quantity 2. wrongType rejects a string quantity. unknownKey rejects currency. nullValue and arrayValue reject non-object argument shapes. malformed rejects invalid JSON. range rejects zero. unknownTool rejects a name outside the registry. wrongCorrelation compares the actual call_id with separately trusted request state. refusal and incomplete stop before argument parsing. changedInput accepts BETA quantity 3 through the same path.

On any rejection, do not execute and do not construct a successful function_call_output. Record a redacted reason, then request a bounded correction or route the case for review. A real mutating tool would additionally need idempotency and tested reconciliation or compensation. This lab is read-only, and its synthetic outputs must never be presented as provider receipts or live prices.

code.label: Verification and recovery checklist
code.code:
[ ] response is completed
[ ] response.error is absent
[ ] typed refusal content is absent
[ ] exactly one expected function_call is selected
[ ] actual call_id is present and matches trusted expectedCallId
[ ] tool name is locally allowlisted
[ ] arguments parse without throwing
[ ] object shape, fields, types, and extra-key policy pass
[ ] ticker membership and quantity range pass locally
[ ] trusted authorization permits the operation
[ ] read-only fixture execution succeeds
[ ] function_call_output uses the actual correlated call_id

Failure at any line -> no execution, no success receipt, bounded recovery

sections.title: Transfer the boundary beyond the exercise
paragraphs: The changed-input case switches ACME quantity 2 to BETA quantity 3. It returns 120 because stocks.json contains a synthetic BETA unitPrice of 40. The same validator, allowlist, correlation, authorization, and execution path handles both inputs. This demonstrates transfer rather than memorization of the ACME result. GAMMA, quantity 0, and quantity 101 must produce DOMAIN rather than an invented value.

For another read-only capability, define a new tool name and schema, add the name to the local registry only after review, and add independent cases for malformed JSON, extra keys, semantic violations, unauthorized context, missing or mismatched call_id, refusal, incomplete responses, provider errors, and changed valid input. Keep raw provider adaptation separate from domain validation.

An optional real workflow would send the provider-shaped request using an authenticated OpenAI API client, inspect the returned lifecycle, adapt a real function_call, run local checks, and submit function_call_output with the matching call_id. Verify the deployment's documentation before doing so. This resource specifies no latest model, SDK version, price, or live result.

sections.title: Sources
paragraphs: OpenAI, Structured Outputs, verified 2026-09-20. The Responses structured-answer shape uses text.format with type json_schema, name, strict, and schema. The guide distinguishes schema-constrained output from JSON-object mode and documents that only a supported subset of JSON Schema is available. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs

OpenAI, Function calling, verified 2026-09-20. The guide documents function_call items, serialized arguments, call_id correlation, and returning function_call_output with the matching call_id. It also supports handling refusal and incomplete outcomes before parsing or execution. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling
